newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian lev falls on dollar demand, seen weaker.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian lev falls on dollar demand, seen weaker.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev fell to 238-242 per dollar in early morning trade from 233 at Wednesday's close, pressured by persistently high foreign currency demand and the longer value date of spot deals, traders said.
"The longer value date traditionally pressures the lev on Thursday but the main reason for the slump is the large foreign currency demand amid low supply," a dealer said.

Banks and clients feverishly sought dollars for short-covering or building up forex positions because of expectations of a further lev fall after last week's cut in the main interest rate, traders said.
But dollar supply was rather low, and was available only at exchange rates as high as 242-245 levs.

"The lev has been constantly losing since last Thursday when it traded near 220 against the dollar and I think it will continue to fall because the central bank could not intervene effectively because of low reserves," a bank dealer said.
The central bank was not seen intervening in support of the lev by 1000 local time (0800 GMT), dealers said.
Bulgaria's forex reserves fell to $506 million at the end of September from $575 million in August because of interest and principal payments on the country's foreign debt.
The central bank cut its main interest rate last Thursday to 20 percent monthly or 240 percent annually from 25 and 300 percent respectively.

The lev is now weaker than its 236-237 per dollar rate on September 23, when the central bank raised its main rate to an all-time high of 300 percent annually from 108 percent to support the fragile lev.
The lev remained stable between 215-220 to the dollar while the record high interest rate was in force until October 18. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
